newsitem.title: USA: COMEX planning trial period for large-scale orders.
newsitem.headline: COMEX planning trial period for large-scale orders.

text.p: COMEX is set to introduce large order executions for copper that will allow a minimum of 40 futures contracts to be dealt in one transaction on an "all-or-nothing" basis, chairman John Moore said on Wednesday.

The move comes as COMEX, a division of the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), tries to raise its volume and open interest levels in the face of competition from rival contracts on the London Metal Exchange.
At its Tuesday meeting, the COMEX copper advisory committee voted to seek NYMEX approval for large order execution for a trial period.
Moore noted the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has already given permission to the Chicago Mercantile Exchange for large-order executions.
Moore said traders being allowed to buy or sell a minimum of 40 lots of copper futures at a single price, in an all-or-nothing deal, would go "hand-in-hand" with copper futures strip trading.
COMEX is set to introduce calendar strip trading in copper futures from September 20.
The issue of large order execution was discussed informally among attendees at the American Copper Council lunch Wednesday in New York.

Some industry players felt large order execution would exclude smaller traders, whilst others argued that 40 lots was too small for large order execution and should perhaps be raised to a minimum of 200 lots.
